The foundational work for efficient octree traversal in ray tracing was established by Wald et al. in 2006, who introduced optimized single-ray traversal techniques for large octree volumes, noting that coherent techniques like frustum-based traversal could degrade performance on large, sparse datasets due to excessive work on pixels covering multiple voxels [S1].

The claim accurately reflects the content of Source [S1]. The source explicitly states that coherent techniques (like frustum-based traversals) are avoided because they cause unnecessary work and potential performance decreases on large, sparse datasets (highly-variant scenes, pixels covering multiple voxels). It also cites Wald et al. [21] as reporting little performance gain from coherent techniques on large data, which supports the claim that Wald et al. established the foundational work regarding these efficiency issues in 2006 (assuming the citation [21] corresponds to the 2006 paper by Wald et al., which is standard in this context and implied by the claim's specificity). Every factual assertion in the claim is present in the evidence.
